s1.syndrome_frame: Palpitations and shortness of breath with a history of arrhythmia
salient_findings: Sustained tachycardia at 122 beats per minute
Regular rhythm with cannon A waves in the jugular venous waveform
ECG showing regular tachycardia with incomplete right bundle branch block morphology
key_facts: 20-year history of palpitations and shortness of breath
Episodes previously controlled with verapamil
Sustained symptoms recurred 6 months before presentation
Not responding to amiodarone therapy
Heart rate: 122 beats per minute
Blood pressure: 135/85 mm Hg
ECG: Regular tachycardia at 130 beats per minute
Incomplete right bundle branch block morphology
QRS duration of 118 milliseconds
Left-axis deviation
3:2 relationship between ventricular and atrial activations
P-wave morphology shows negative deflection in leads II and aVF
24-hour Holter monitor: Sustained tachycardia throughout monitoring period
Echocardiogram: Results within normal limits

shortlist.label: Atrial Flutter
shortlist.why_kept: Regular tachycardia with 3:2 relationship between ventricular and atrial activations

shortlist.label: Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: History of palpitations and shortness of breath with previous response to verapamil

shortlist.label: Orthodromic Atrioventricular Reentrant Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Sustained tachycardia with incomplete right bundle branch block morphology

shortlist.label: Supraventricular Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Regular rhythm with cannon A waves in the jugular venous waveform

shortlist.label: Atrial Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: P-wave morphology shows negative deflection in leads II and aVF

raw.rationale: The ECG shows regular tachycardia with a 3:2 relationship between ventricular and atrial activations, and P-wave morphology with negative deflection in leads II and aVF, which is consistent with atrial flutter.

rejected.label: Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia
rejected.why: AVNRT typically has a 1:1 atrioventricular relationship, not 3:2

rejected.label: Orthodromic Atrioventricular Reentrant Tachycardia
rejected.why: Orthodromic AVRT typically has a 1:1 atrioventricular relationship and a narrower QRS complex

rejected.label: Supraventricular Tachycardia
rejected.why: SVT is a broad term that encompasses several types of tachycardia, but the specific ECG findings point more specifically to atrial flutter

rejected.label: Atrial Tachycardia
rejected.why: Atrial tachycardia typically has a 1:1 atrioventricular relationship and P-wave morphology that is different from the negative deflection in leads II and aVF seen in this case
